accepted.cause: First nine months net revenues up 8% with margin improvement
accepted.effect: pre-tax margin expansion to 33.1% drives fundamental valuation upside
accepted.evidence_span: Highlights • Goldman Sachs reported first nine months net revenues of $24.24 billion, 8% higher than the first nine months of 2016, which contributed to a 230 basis point improvement in pre-tax margin to 33.1%.

accepted.cause: Investing & Lending revenues reach three-year high
accepted.effect: strongest quarterly performance in three years reinforces growth narrative
accepted.evidence_span: Investing & Lending generated net revenues of $1.88 billion, its highest quarterly performance in over three years.

accepted.cause: Debt underwriting revenues hit nine-month high
accepted.effect: record leveraged finance revenue supports estimate revision upside
accepted.evidence_span: Debt underwriting produced year-to-date net revenues of $2.03 billion, its highest for the first nine months of the year, reflecting a leading position for the firm’s leveraged finance franchise.

accepted.cause: Commissions and fees revenues declined due to lower volumes
accepted.effect: lower market volumes in US compress commission revenue expectations
accepted.evidence_span: Net revenues from commissions and fees were lower, reflecting lower market volumes in the United States, and net revenues in securities services were slightly higher compared with the third quarter of 2016.
